Notorious criminals of both collar varieties that are somehow stupid enough to keep surrounding themselves with faulty machinery, poisonable food,  and an incompetent, half blind guard force. Yet these glaringly stupid ai characters still feel remarkably human, as they comment on the world around them, the world that you help shape with your discreet murders. Corporations such as Ether are first seen as producers of the poisons 47 can bring into a mission, but reappear throughout the series. In fact, you can even assassinate two Ether employees, Silvio Caruso and Francesca De-Santis in the legacy pack DLC. Opportunities to kill your targets are full of lore tidbits, and culminate in some grimly satisfying murders that ooze irony as much as they do blood. But sometimes, you don't even want to hit some men (and women too, 47 doesn't discriminate with his brutal murders.) the maps are chock full of easter eggs, amazing sights, and npcs that are just full of character, even if they exist mainly to set up a mission story. It really isn't hard to just put yourself in 47's expensive shoes and enjoy listening to the music as a member of the Ark Society, or maybe just stand around in a stupid flamingo costume with the stone cold face of a hardened killer. It's really an amazing game to just mess around with, and I would easily recommend the entire World of Assassination trilogy to any fans of the stealth and sandbox genres.

Hitman 2 is the latest assignment for everyone’s favourite bald assassin, Agent 47, and directly continues the story from the previous game.

The Good

•	Stealth focused gameplay will feel familiar to fans of the series. Use a variety of environmental distractions to lure NPCs to areas where there are no witnesses, incapacitate them, hide the body and disguise yourself with their uniform to gain access to restricted areas without raising suspicion, eventually getting close enough to eliminate your target.
•	Every mission has been designed with multiple ways to assassinate your targets. Explore the area and listen to conversations to trigger story missions, where you can acquire a unique disguise from a character your target plans to meet alone, or find an opportunity to sabotage the environment resulting in an accident. Or, just watch their routine, identify a location where they’re vulnerable, and ambush them with a remote explosive, poison their food, or simply shoot them and run away.
•	I really appreciated the amount of player freedom built into the level design when I replayed each mission. This includes unlocking different starting locations and items as you gain XP from completing challenges.
•	Every location feels alive, with so much detail in the environment that isn’t even connected to the story, from large crowds at a sporting event to just a random jogger in a suburban area.
•	Voice acting is mostly good.
•	Controls are fully rebindable and work great with mouse and keyboard.
•	If you already own Hitman 1, those missions are added into this game for free.

The Questionable

•	There are lots of bonus missions like Escalations and Contracts, but whether they’re good or bad depends on your point of view. I personally don’t enjoy them because they usually have restrictions like killing the target with a specific weapon or while wearing a specific disguise, or there might be a time limit. Basically the exact opposite of the freedom you get in the main story missions.

The Bad

•	Cutscenes are just still images with dialogue, which looks weird if you play Hitman 1 and 2 back to back because the previous game had fully animated cutscenes.
•	Elusive targets are still time limited. I agree with only having one chance to play each mission because its a test of your skill, and completing them is like a badge of honour. But we should be able to make that attempt at any time. And its not fair that if you wait to buy the game, you’ve already missed several elusive target missions.
•	You have to be online at all times, and if your connection to Steam drops even for a moment, the game pauses and threatens to return you to the main menu unless you reconnect. Fortunately there are frequent auto saves and you can manually save at any time (depending on difficulty level), so you won’t lose much progress if you can’t reconnect, but its still annoying to suddenly have this message pop up, and we really shouldn’t need to worry about this in a singleplayer game.

The Recommendation

Hitman 2 is a fun game with high quality production values, which you should definitely play if you’re a fan of the franchise, or enjoy stealth games in general. However the standard purchase price is really high, and of course there’s a season pass, so perhaps wait for a sale.

This game is not one that you should pick up, play and then forget once you've completed the story. It's one that really encourages you to play through multiple times and explore a level on various occasions, so that you can discover every nook and cranny. The main motivation to revisit a level is to follow the different mission stories, as well as to complete the sundry challenges, and find anything else you may have missed on previous playthroughs (e.g. rooms, NPC dialogue etc.) The content doesn't stop at just the main missions; some locations may have extra "special assignments" (mini missions), and there are "elusive targets" (missions that are available only for a limited time, and where you can kill the target just once) and contracts. Contracts are made by other players, where targets different to those from the main story can be killed, often requiring certain conditions to be completed (e.g. wear a specific disguise when you kill a target). In addition to contracts, there are also escalations, similar to contracts except they are officially included in the game and need to be finished on three occasions, each occasion requiring new conditions to be met and/or adding new targets to be eliminated.

One of the most rewarding things about this game is setting yourself a goal to fulfill on the main missions (especially attaining silent assassin) or completing particularly tough contracts or escalations. As you roam around you'll find more items and remember where they are, find quicker ways to get to a target and leave, know where NPCs are and what their routine is etc. Combine this growing knowledge with tenacity and you'll soon learn how to finish off a target and then escape swiftly and stealthily. After all, Hitman is really just a puzzle game; you gallivant around a level and learn every little thing about it before devising a good strategy.

If you want a game that challenges you but also rewards you for exploration, consider this one. It's great fun, and it's jam-packed with content, especially if you buy the DLC and the legacy pack. Be warned though, it's big, especially since it includes Hitman 2016.
